title: Attention to Mamba: A Recipe for Cross-Architecture Distillation
gist: An Apple TMLR paper proposes a two-stage recipe for distilling a pretrained Transformer into an Attention-free Mamba model: first into linearized attention via the kernel trick, then into an adapted Mamba with principled initialization. The distilled model nearly matches the Pythia-1B teacher in perplexity (14.01 vs 13.86) but still trails on in-context-recall tasks.

insights.claim: State Space Models such as Mamba are gaining adoption as Transformer alternatives because they use less memory and give higher throughput at generation than attention-based models.
insights.speaker: Apple ML Research
insights.so_what: Lower inference memory and higher throughput point to cheaper serving and on-device generation, which is relevant to inference hardware and edge AI demand.

insights.claim: Distilling pretrained Transformers into Mamba-like architectures is a way to adopt SSMs while reusing the large stock of pretrained Transformer models and accumulated Transformer training know-how.
insights.speaker: Apple ML Research
insights.so_what: Converting existing checkpoints instead of pretraining from scratch lowers the cost of switching architectures.

insights.claim: Prior work found that naive distillation from a Transformer into Mamba fails to preserve the teacher's performance, which pushed the field toward hybrid models mixing attention and SSM blocks.
insights.speaker: Apple ML Research
insights.so_what: Challenges the assumption that hybrids are necessary; pure-SSM students would keep the full efficiency benefit.

insights.claim: Apple researchers argue that giving Mamba a principled initialization is the key to a better cross-architecture distillation recipe that needs no attention blocks.
insights.speaker: Apple ML Research
insights.so_what: Initialization, not architecture hybridization, may be the lever for low-cost conversion of Transformers into efficient models.
insights.quote: by equipping Mamba with a principled initialization, we can recover an overall better recipe for cross-architectural distillation
insights.locator: The key argument from our work

insights.claim: The proposed recipe first distills a Transformer into a linearized-attention model using an adaptation of the kernel trick, then distills that linearized model into an adapted Mamba model containing no attention block.
insights.speaker: Apple ML Research
insights.so_what: Linear attention as an intermediate step is a reusable path for moving pretrained models onto subquadratic architectures.
insights.locator: we propose a principled two-stage approach

insights.claim: A Mamba model distilled from a Pythia-1B Transformer reaches a perplexity of 14.01, close to the teacher's 13.86.
insights.speaker: Apple ML Research
insights.so_what: Near-parity perplexity at 1B scale suggests attention-free students can replace Transformers in cost-sensitive deployments.

insights.claim: The distilled Mamba model's quality largely carries over to downstream tasks, but gaps remain on tasks that depend more on in-context recall, a known SSM weakness relative to attention.
insights.speaker: Apple ML Research
insights.so_what: In-context recall is the area to watch: retrieval-heavy and long-context uses may still favor attention or hybrid models.

insights.claim: The recipe was validated with ablations at 1B parameters on 10B tokens across sequence-mixer architectures, plus scaling analyses over model size, total distillation tokens and token allocation between the two stages.
insights.speaker: Apple ML Research
insights.so_what: The evidence is at small scale (1B parameters, 10B tokens); whether it holds at frontier scale has not been shown.
